thread_analysis.thread_summary: This thread mixes internal lab-operations coordination at [COMPANY] (Bluetooth SIG test lab/consultant) for [COMPANY]'s 19AVN/UXC-family products with later customer-facing registration review for the 19AVNJ model. The first half covers RF and RF PHY test troubleshooting at InterLab -- a connector-reseat retest protocol, correct DUT test-mode procedure selection for an Infineon-based chipset, and a multi-message diagnosis of which apps and PCs can safely coexist on the InterLab control PC during active RF PHY testing -- plus PTS test-media preparation for an AVRCP profile test item. The second half covers a customer registration review for 19AVNJ: correcting which Controller Subsystem and Host Stack QDIDs should be referenced to avoid an Inter-Layer Dependency (IDL) caused by a Bluetooth Core spec version mismatch, clarifying profile-naming and non-implementation documentation (HID vs HID11, HOGP removal), the post-registration compliance-folder document checklist, and administrative payment/model-name corrections.
all_questions_found: Given the RF test result was uncertain, what physical/connector verification and targeted RF/RF PHY retest steps should be performed before concluding the RF test failed?
Is the connector-verification protocol's intermediate step necessary, or can it be skipped in favor of the final RF PHY differential step?
For an Infineon-chipset DUT tested via InterLab automation, which DUT test-mode procedure applies to SIG certification RF/RF PHY testing, and is an external PC required to issue these commands?
Can the same control PC be used both to control InterLab's measurement instruments and to run the DUT-mode-entry application for the device under test?
Why did reusing the InterLab control PC for a LAN-connected status application cause TCP-client and connectivity problems during RF PHY testing on one model?
What troubleshooting steps should be taken when the RF PHY bridge-app PC and DUT cannot establish the expected Bluetooth LE Direct Mode connection?
How should test media files be set up in the PTS Playlist folder for the AVRCP profile test item, while preserving the originals?
For the registration, should the Controller Subsystem QDID referenced in the quote request be replaced with an already-registered QDID at a newer Core spec version for the same module?

Why does Including the quote-requested Host Stack + Profile QDID together with the recommended Controller Subsystem QDID generate Inter-Layer Dependencies (IDL) between GAP and LL, and should this be resolved with a TCW or by changing the referenced Host Stack QDID?

In the registration quote request, does one profile abbreviation refer to the same test item as its numbered variant, and should a profile's removal from the quote be read as intentional non-implementation rather than an omission?
What product documentation needs to be assembled for the post-registration compliance folder?
Is a trailing punctuation character in the requested model name an error that should be corrected before registration?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The thread illustrates several distinct test-stage and registration-stage mechanics: ruling out a flaky physical RF connection before treating an RF test as a real failure; selecting the correct DUT test-mode procedure (open-loop regulatory testing vs. certification-lab automation) for a given chipset vendor's documentation; understanding which auxiliary applications can share a certification lab's control PC without interfering with its continuous instrument-control duties during RF PHY testing; preparing PTS playlist test media for a profile test item; and diagnosing an Inter-Layer Dependency (IDL) caused by Including QDIDs built on mismatched Bluetooth Core spec versions across the Controller and Host/Profile layers.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: Several threads of reasoning recur: (1) an inconclusive or failing RF result should first be checked against a physical/connector-seating explanation via a defined reseat-and-retest protocol before being treated as a genuine non-compliance; (2) DUT test-mode procedures differ by purpose (regulatory open-loop vs. certification-lab automation) and the correct one must be matched to the testing context; (3) apps that run continuously during a measurement (protocol-bridge apps) must not share a PC with the lab's own instrument-control duties, while apps that only run before testing starts can safely coexist; (4) an Inter-Layer Dependency between GAP and LL arises when the Included Host/Profile QDID's Core spec version supports capabilities (e.g., Isochronous, advanced Advertising) that the Included Controller QDID's earlier-version LL ICS does not have entries for -- the fix is to match Core spec versions across Included QDIDs rather than seek a waiver for the mismatch.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Treating an RF result as a genuine failure without first ruling out a connector-seating issue risks unnecessary re-testing or an incorrect failure conclusion reported to the customer. Using the wrong DUT test-mode procedure or sharing the InterLab control PC with a during-test bridge application risks test setup failures and lost lab time diagnosing connectivity problems that stem from configuration rather than the DUT itself. Including a Host Stack QDID whose Core spec version is mismatched with the Controller QDID risks an Inter-Layer Dependency that blocks registration unless resolved -- pursuing a TCW for a version mismatch that is itself questionable risks rejection, where simply referencing a same-version Host Stack QDID avoids the problem entirely.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: An earlier round of correspondence (referenced but not shown in this thread) had recommended applying for a TCW (ES-26007) to cover the GAP-LL Inter-Layer Dependency; this was superseded once the consultant identified that the underlying cause was a Core spec version mismatch between Controller and Host Stack QDIDs, at which point the TCW route was withdrawn as unlikely to succeed and replaced with a recommendation to reference a matching-version Host Stack QDID instead.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When Including multiple QDIDs into one registration produces an Inter-Layer Dependency, check whether the Included QDIDs were built against different Bluetooth Core spec versions before assuming a waiver (TCW) is the right fix -- a version mismatch is often better resolved by referencing a same-version QDID for one of the layers than by trying to waive the resulting dependency. Separately, when diagnosing an RF/RF PHY test or lab-equipment problem, first rule out physical connection issues and control-PC/application placement conflicts before treating the result as a true DUT defect.
